title: The Big Five
objective: After this level you can explain the five personality traits psychologists measure and what each one describes.
summary: Most psychologists describe personality with five traits, OCEAN. Each is a dial on which most people sit midway, usually measured by self-report, and the five appear across 50 cultures.

cards.headline: The dictionary holds about 4,500 words for what a person is like.
cards.body: In 1936 Gordon Allport and Henry Odbert combed an English dictionary for words that describe lasting personality traits, and found about 4,500 of them. Shy, careful, bossy, warm: the list goes on and on. Could a pile that big boil down to a few basics?

cards.headline: Five dials, not five boxes
cards.body: Today the most popular answer in personality psychology is the Five Factor Model, or Big Five. Its traits spell OCEAN: openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism. Everyone has all five. Each runs along a spectrum, and most of us sit somewhere midway rather than at either end. So you aren't simply an extravert or not; you sit somewhere on the extraversion dial.

items.label: Feelings
points: Neuroticism: a tendency to feel negative emotions

cards.headline: How the dials get read
cards.body: Traits are usually measured with a self-report inventory: statements you rate from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree). The catch is that people may answer in ways that look good. The five aren't just an English-language quirk, either. In a 2005 study led by Robert McCrae, students in 50 cultures rated someone they knew well, and the five-factor pattern was recognizable in all 50.

cards.headline: The Big Five
learned: Five traits: openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism
Each trait is a dial; most people sit midway

questions.prompt: Which Big Five trait describes a tendency to feel negative emotions?

options.label: Openness
options.rationale: Openness covers imagination, feelings and ideas.

options.label: Agreeableness
options.rationale: Agreeableness means being cooperative and good-natured.

questions.explanation: Neuroticism is the Big Five trait for a tendency to experience negative emotions.

questions.prompt: Priya is self-disciplined and never misses a deadline, but she is quiet at parties. How would the Big Five describe her?

options.label: As a conscientious type, with no extraversion score
options.rationale: Everyone has all five traits, each on a spectrum.

options.label: High on conscientiousness, lower on extraversion
High on neuroticism and openness
options.rationale: Nothing described points to negative emotions or imagination.

options.label: High on agreeableness, high on extraversion
options.rationale: Being quiet at parties suggests lower extraversion.

questions.explanation: Self-discipline and meeting deadlines mark conscientiousness; quietness at parties suggests a lower setting on the extraversion dial.

questions.prompt: Big Five scores usually come from self-report inventories. Which weakness of self-reports from Level 8 could skew them?

options.label: They can only include a few people
options.rationale: Surveys make it easy to reach large numbers of people.

options.label: They prove cause and effect too easily
options.rationale: Only experiments show cause and effect.

options.label: People may answer in ways that make them look good

questions.explanation: Self-reports can be skewed because people lie, misremember or answer to look good, and personality inventories share that risk.
